messages.author: 1f9042b5c10ebe6d
messages.subject: Facet wrap labels
parts:
Hello-
I am using facet_wrap to plot multiple histograms by a variable called
"group1". However, I want to label each plot by a different variable
("species"). I can't facet by species, because some species appear
more than once (i.e., belong to more than one group). I can't figure
out how to change the labels on the individual plots- must they be the
faceting variable?

Example:

library(ggplot2)
group1 <- sample(c("1", "2", "3", "4"), 100, replace=T)
species <- sample(c("x", "y"), 200, replace=T)
myvalues <- rnorm(400)
df <- data.frame(group1, species, myvalues)


m<- ggplot(df, aes(myvalues) )
m<-m + geom_histogram(aes(y=..density..))
m<-m+ facet_wrap(~group1)
print(m)

this creates the histograms as I want them, grouped how I want them. I
just can't change the labels to species, and I don't want to resort to
doing it by hand!

Thanks,
Gretchen

messages.subject: RE: Facet wrap labels
parts:
Hi

Sorry, in my effort to make the example more simple than my real problem, I obscured what the actual problem was.  In my actual dataset, I have 70 groups.  The groups represent different species collected using different methods.  So, some species are represented by only one group, while others are represented by multiple groups.  I want separate histograms for each group, but I want to label them by species.  The figure produced using facet_wrap(~group1) shows the data exactly as I want them, I just want to replace the labels with the species names (instead of the group number) without having to do it by hand.

Maybe I just need to change all the groups to something containing the species name, but it would be much easier to just change the labels if I can!

Thanks

Gretchen
